subject.title: [Enhancement] High I/O Overhead from Synchronous Permission Hardening on State DB Commit Hot Path

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a lifecycle-aware optimization that removes unconditional post-write chmod calls while preserving private modes for every newly created SQLite sidecar?
rationale: The redundant work is real and shipped, but deciding when permission checks may safely be skipped changes a credentials-adjacent security invariant and cannot be resolved from the unmeasured performance claim alone.

options.title: Benchmark then optimize lifecycle
options.body: Require before-and-after latency measurements, then deduplicate hardening with explicit main/WAL/SHM/journal mode tests and no broader EPERM tolerance.

options.title: Retain current hardening
options.body: Keep unconditional post-write checks until measured impact shows that added lifecycle complexity is justified.

options.title: Unify permission policy work
options.body: Design this together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102912 as a single reviewed SQLite sidecar permission lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Benchmark then optimize lifecycle
recommendation.body: Require before-and-after latency measurements, then deduplicate hardening with explicit main/WAL/SHM/journal mode tests and no broader EPERM tolerance.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the recent permission, sidecar, and state database lifecycle history needed to define a safe skip-and-recheck contract.
